info.title: Drupflare Dashboard API
info.description: The HTTP API behind the Drupflare dashboard. Every operation names the permission it checks in x-action and its rate class in x-rate-class.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, sign-out and passkey and provider flows.

tags.name: me
tags.description: The signed-in account, its sessions and devices.

tags.name: delegations
tags.description: Agency access to a client organisation.

tags.name: api-keys
tags.description: API keys for scripts and integrations.

tags.name: sites
tags.description: Sites and everything that belongs to one.

tags.name: planes
tags.description: Planes a site can run on.

tags.name: billing
tags.description: Plans, invoices and the billing portal.

tags.name: clients
tags.description: Client organisations managed by an agency.

tags.name: access-reviews
tags.description: Access reviews, stale credentials and evidence.

tags.name: service-accounts
tags.description: Service accounts that hold keys and no sign-in.

tags.name: gate
tags.description: Visitor access to private sites and environments.

get.description: Abuse reports newest first, optionally only those in one state. Metadata and the reviewer notes; never site content.

post.summary: Open an abuse report on a site
post.description: Records a concern about a site so it can be reviewed. The site must exist. The public report form is not part of this route.

put.summary: Move an abuse report to another state
put.description: Moves a report between open, reviewing, actioned and dismissed. Actioned and dismissed are final. Answers 409 for a move the states do not allow.

post.summary: Suspend the site of an abuse report
post.description: Suspends the reported site through the site authority, tells the organization owners by email, records both audit logs and closes the report as actioned. A repeat for the same report returns the same operation. A dismissed report answers 409.

get.description: Changes an administrator made that belong to no organisation, such as the global automatic repair switch, newest first. Page with the id of the last row you have.

post.summary: Start break-glass access to an organization
post.description: Opens one hour of access to an organization without a support grant. Needs step-up and a written reason. Every owner of the organization is emailed at once, both audit logs record the reason, and one admin can start it only a few times a day.

get.description: Cloudflare credit balance, billable usage by service, account headroom, and the work in flight. The Cloudflare reads are cached for 60 seconds. Needs the admin role and a Cloudflare Access login.
The saved read-only statements, newest first. Needs step-up.

post.description: Saves a statement under a name. The statement has to pass the same check as a typed one. Needs step-up.

delete.description: Removes a saved statement. The audit log keeps the record of who saved it. Needs step-up.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.description: Runs one SELECT on one shard or on all of them. Only a single SELECT passes: no comments, no second statement, no write, PRAGMA, ATTACH or WITH, and only a short list of functions. The result stops at 200 rows and 5 seconds. Secret columns are refused by name. Every statement is audited with its text and the admin. Needs step-up.

get.description: The shards the read-only console can query, with their size in bytes and, when a table is named, its row count on each shard. Needs step-up.
Every platform switch with its value and who set it last. A switch nobody has set reads as off.

put.description: Turns one platform switch on or off. Needs step-up. The change is audited with the admin who made it. Turning ladder.auto on or off needs the confirmation word.

get.summary: Read the repair catalogue and the automatic repair switches
get.description: The catalogue rows, with whether each can run today and why not, and the switches that turn automatic repair off or on for a site, an organisation or everything.

put.summary: Turn automatic repair on or off
put.description: Sets the automatic repair switch for a site, an organisation or everything. The global switch needs the confirmation word. A scope id that matches nothing is refused.

get.summary: Read the mail categories and the notification switch
get.description: The mail categories, essential or optional, and whether optional mail is paused. The send log for the current UTC day: mail sent, failed and skipped, by count only, with the daily send cap. The log holds no address and no body.
The newest operations first across every shard: type, status, verification and, for a failed one, the plain reason it stopped. The filter narrows to operations in flight or failed.
The newest organizations first across every shard. A name search matches any part of the name.
Metadata for one organisation: its member count, sites by state, plan and subscription state. Notification activity is not recorded yet. Never site content.

Counts of users, organisations, sites by state and operations by status, plus the cards on the admin front page: operations in flight and failed, open abuse reports, the switches that are on, and the release rollout running now. Needs the admin role and a Cloudflare Access login.
The releases of one kind, newest first, each with its latest rollout when it has one.

post.summary: Register a release from its manifest
post.description: Fetches the manifest at the address, checks it against the digest and stores the release. A repeat of the same release changes nothing. The signed release event uses the same check.

get.summary: Read the latest rollout of a release
get.description: The ring the rollout is in, how many sites each ring holds, what stopped it and why, and the time from the advisory to the last ring reached.

post.summary: Roll a release out across the fleet
post.description: Sends the release to every live site, ring by ring. The next ring starts only when the one before it reads clean, and a bad reading stops the rollout. Needs a recent step-up. Send an Idempotency-Key header. Answers 409 while another rollout is running.

post.summary: Stop a rollout before its next ring
post.description: Asks the rollout to stop. Rings that already received the release keep it; the next ring never starts. Answers 409 when the rollout has ended.

get.description: The newest sites first across every shard. Metadata only, never site content.

post.summary: Lift the suspension on a site
post.description: Makes a suspended site active again through the site authority. Needs step-up. The owners are told by email and both audit logs record it. Only a suspension lifts: a revoked site stays revoked.

get.summary: List live support grants and break-glass starts
get.description: Support grants that are live now, soonest to end first, and the recent break-glass starts with their reasons. Metadata only.

post.description: Starts a build of a template at the commit the corpus pins now. The build installs the template once and stores the result, so a new site can start from it. A second build of the same template is refused while one is running.

get.description: Lists drafts, published and retired trust documents with their hashes.

post.summary: Upload a trust document as a draft
post.description: Stores one file as a draft. The file is PDF, DOCX, Markdown or plain text, up to 10 MB. Publish it to show it on the trust center.
Shows a draft on the trust center. The change is written to the platform audit log.
Removes a published document from the trust center. The file stays in storage. The change is written to the platform audit log.

get.description: The newest users first: address, name, platform role and when they joined. Never a credential or a session.

post.description: Sends a six-digit code to the address. A new address creates an account when the code is verified. The same answer comes back for every address.
Signs in with the code and sets the session cookie. The body never carries the session token.
Ends the session named by the cookie and clears it. A missing session still succeeds.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.summary: List the provider sign-ins that are set up
get.description: Names the providers whose client id and secret are both configured, so the sign-in screen shows only buttons that can work.

Checks the state against the cookie, exchanges the code and signs in. A provider email that matches an existing account never signs in or merges: the answer is link_required, and the person confirms the link from that account in settings.

Returns the provider address to send the browser to, and sets a short-lived cookie that ties the callback to this browser. The request carries state and a PKCE challenge, and asks for name and email only.

post.description: Returns the options to pass to navigator.credentials.get. The challenge works once and expires after five minutes.
Verifies the signed challenge and sets the session cookie. Every failure answers the same way.

get.description: The address the identity provider sends the browser back to. It checks the state against the cookie, exchanges the code, checks the token and the email domain, and signs in, creating the account and membership on the first visit. An address that already has an account never merges: the browser goes on to confirm the link from that account. Every answer is a redirect.

Sends the browser to the identity provider of the organisation with this sign-in name. The request carries state, a nonce and a PKCE challenge, and a short-lived cookie ties the return to this browser.

post.description: Takes a fresh sign-in code for the signed-in address, marks the session as recently authenticated and rotates the session cookie.

Buys an add-on as a subscription, billed with the plan, or as a one-time pack. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys. A subscription add-on on a running subscription changes at once and answers applied; otherwise a hosted checkout opens and the answer is its url. The quantity changes only when the payment provider confirms it. An add-on that does not exist, is not on sale or has an unreviewed price answers 404.

put.description: Sets how many of an add-on the organisation holds on its running subscription; 0 removes it. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys. An add-on the organisation does not hold answers 404. The quantity changes only when the payment provider confirms it.

post.description: Opens a hosted checkout for a managed plan. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys. Plans whose price has not been reviewed answer 404. An organisation with no billing contact, name or country answers 422 until it saves them. An organisation whose running subscription holds add-ons alone gets the plan added to it and the answer is applied.

put.description: Saves the billing contact name and email and the billing country that a checkout or an add-on purchase needs. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys. The checkout page asks for the full address and keeps these in step.

post.description: Opens the hosted portal where the organisation changes its card, reads invoices or cancels. Needs a signed-in session and refuses API keys.

get.description: Lists what can be bought on top of a plan, as a subscription, a one-time pack or both. Prices follow the same review rule as plans, and an add-on that is not on sale carries the reason.

Lists the plans with what each includes. A price appears only after it has been reviewed, and platform administrators see every price. A null figure is unknown or negotiated, and sitesUnlimited marks a plan with no site limit.

post.description: Marks a contact verified from the one-time link in its confirmation mail. The link works once and lasts seven days.
Joins the organization with the role the invitation offers. The invitation is used up by this call, and the signed-in address must match the one it was sent to. An API key is refused.
Shows the organization and role an invitation offers, and whether it was sent to the signed-in address. The token goes in the body so it stays out of logs. An API key is refused.

get.description: Returns the account behind the session or, for an API key, the account that issued it.
Lists the provider identities linked to your account. The email code is always available and is not listed.

delete.description: Removes a linked provider identity. It needs a fresh authentication and refuses to remove your last sign-in method.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Checks the state against the cookie and against this session, exchanges the code and connects the provider account to the signed-in account. It needs a fresh authentication. A provider account that is already connected, here or to another account, is a conflict.

post.description: Returns the provider address to send the browser to, and sets a short-lived cookie that ties the callback to this browser. The state records who started it, so only this session can finish the connection. It needs a fresh authentication.
Links the provider identity from the last provider sign-in in this browser to your account. It needs a fresh authentication, and the provider email must match your account email.

get.description: Lists the optional mail you can switch on or off, with each switch on until you turn it off, and the mail that always sends. Essential mail has no switch.

put.description: Switches optional mail on or off for the signed-in account. It works from a browser session only, never with an API key. Essential mail cannot be switched off, and naming it is refused.

get.description: Lists the organisations you belong to, the personal organisation first and then by name. A key lists the organisations of the person who issued it, and only when its scopes allow account.read.
Lists your registered passkeys, newest first. Keys and counters are never returned.

patch.description: Changes the label of one of your passkeys. It does not need a fresh authentication.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

delete.description: Removes one of your passkeys. It needs a fresh authentication and refuses to remove your last sign-in method.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.description: Two calls, both needing a fresh authentication. Phase options returns the creation options. Phase verify checks the new credential against that challenge and stores it.

get.description: Lists the signed-in devices, newest first. A person holds only a handful of sessions, so the list is never paged.

delete.description: Ends every session except the one making this request. It needs a fresh authentication.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

delete.description: Ends one of your sessions. Revoking another session needs a fresh authentication. Revoking the session you are using needs none and also clears its cookie.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.summary: Claim a pairing from a box
post.description: Takes the claim token a signed-in owner created, pins the box public key and answers with the node id, the link address and the dashboard public key. A token works once and for 15 minutes. The token is the proof, so the request carries no signature.

get.description: Lists the API keys of the organisation in the path, newest first: the name, the public prefix, the permissions, and when each was created, last used and expires or was revoked. The secret is shown once, when the key is created, and never again.

post.description: Creates a key for the organisation in the path and returns its token once. The key can hold only permissions that you hold yourself and that a key can carry, and it loses any permission you lose. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.
Stops a key from working at once. The next request that carries it is refused. Revoking a key that is already revoked changes nothing. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Lists the estate assessments of the organisation, newest first.

post.description: Reads an inventory of sites, given as CSV with a header row or as JSON, and starts one read-only check for every site it names. Rows that cannot be read are counted and left out; a file that cannot be read at all is refused. A site is checked from the outside with the same public check as the preflight. Sites on a server whose key is listed in credentialIds are also surveyed over SSH, read only. Only a few sites on a domain whose ownership is not proven are checked. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same assessment.

get.description: Returns one assessment with its state, the number of rows in each state and class, and the report once it has finished.

post.description: Stops an assessment that is still running. Sites already checked keep their results, and the rest are marked skipped. An assessment that has finished cannot be cancelled.

get.description: Streams every row of the assessment as one CSV file. The inventory columns come first, so the file can be uploaded again as an inventory. Effort is written as Not estimated.

get.summary: List the rows of an assessment
get.description: Lists the sites of an assessment in row order, with the class, state and findings of each. Filter by class, by state, or by text in the hostname.

post.description: Reads the inventory in the body the way an assessment would and returns how many rows and sites it holds, which rows were left out and why, and which columns were ignored. Nothing is stored and no site is contacted.

post.summary: Get the record that proves a domain
post.description: Returns the TXT record and the file text that prove the organisation controls a domain. The value belongs to this organisation and this domain, and is not a site record. A domain with a proof on file comes back with proven set.

Looks for the proof of a domain, in DNS or in the file on the site, and records the domain as proven for the organisation when it finds it. The file is read from the domain over https through the public address guard.

get.description: Reads the organisation spend budget: the percent of the monthly allowance, whether it blocks or only alerts, the allowance, the views counted so far (a lower bound), the current state and the alerts already sent this month. A free organisation has no budget and the answer is not_applicable. The enforcement flag says whether blocking is on or still in shadow mode, where it logs and alerts but blocks nothing.

put.description: Sets the organisation spend budget. Lowering it, or switching from alert to block, needs the billing permission. Raising it, or switching from block to alert, also needs a fresh sign-in. Every change is audited with the old and new values. The response says how soon the change reaches the sites.

get.description: Lists the client workspaces of this agency with the sites grouped under each one and the contacts for incidents, migrations, refunds and restores.

post.description: Adds a client to this agency. Record who the end customer contacts for incidents, migrations, refunds and restores, and any contract notes the team needs.

put.description: Replaces the name, contacts and notes of a client workspace. The sites under it do not change here.

delete.description: Removes a client workspace and its grouping. The sites stay in the organisation and are not changed.

get.summary: Export a client usage as CSV
get.description: Downloads the views of each site under a client, one row per site and month, for the months given. Unaccounted hours are counted apart from views. Up to 24 months at a time.

get.summary: List the contacts of an organisation
get.description: Lists the technical, billing, legal and recovery contacts that are set. A role with no contact is missing from the list.

put.summary: Set a technical, billing or legal contact
put.description: Sets the name and address of one contact. A new address starts unverified until it is confirmed. The recovery contact has its own route, which needs step-up.

post.summary: Send a test notification to a contact
post.description: Sends one real test mail, in the operational notice category, to a verified contact that is set to receive notifications. The answer says what happened in plain words.

post.summary: Send a confirmation to a contact
post.description: Emails the contact a one-time link. The link lasts seven days and works once. Confirming it marks the address verified.

put.description: Sets the recovery contact. Owners only, and only after a fresh sign-in. A new address starts unverified.

get.summary: Search the verified corpus of Drupal codebases
get.description: Lists the codebases in the verified corpus with their status, whether each one can be installed and the reason when it cannot. Filter by part of the name or by status.

get.summary: List the cost centers of an organisation
get.description: Lists the cost centers of the organisation, by code. A cost center holds billing only and never grants access.

post.description: Adds a cost center. The code is unique within the organisation and is the name finance knows the center by.

put.description: Replaces the code, name, department and owner contact of a cost center. Sites keep their assignment.

get.summary: Download the monthly cost report as CSV
get.description: Streams the cost report of one month as CSV, one row per cost center and a central total. Text cells that start with a formula character are prefixed with an apostrophe.

Shows the usage of each cost center for one month with its accounting state, an optional allocation of an organisation total by share, a straight-line projection and a central summary. A projection is a line through the views so far, not a forecast.

get.summary: List sites and their cost centers
get.description: Lists the live sites of the organisation with the cost center each one bills to.

put.summary: Assign a site to a cost center
put.description: Sets the one cost center a site bills to, or clears it. The technical and business owner names are kept on the site, and an omitted name is left as it was.

post.description: Takes a built Worker as a .tar.gz request body (Content-Type application/gzip) and returns what the platform made of it. The archive holds a wrangler.jsonc at its top level, the built entry file that wrangler.jsonc names as main, any other built modules next to it and the assets directory it names. The archive is capped at 16 MiB and 40 MiB unpacked, with at most 20,000 entries, and it may hold no absolute path, no .. path and no link; each of those is refused with 422. The answer lists findings, each with a stable code and a severity, and whether the bundle is deployable. A deployable bundle is stored and gets a bundleId, which Create a site and Update a custom site accept. A bundle with a blocking finding is not stored and has a null bundleId. The same archive uploaded twice gives the same bundleId. The bundle is read, never run. Refused with 403 when the plan does not include custom code; the answer names the plan that does. Do not send an Idempotency-Key header; an upload is repeatable on its own.

get.description: Lists the agency access this organisation has given, and the access it has received as an agency. Access to several sites is one entry.

post.description: Offers an agency access to this organisation as a maintainer or a viewer, to chosen sites or to all sites, with an optional expiry. The agency has to accept before it can act. Nothing changes for the agency until then.

Lets this agency act for the client organisation within the role and sites the client chose. The agency sees its own role limits on top of the access. Accepting twice, or after the access ended or expired, is refused.

Ends the agency access at once, from either side. The agency loses every action it had through the access, and both organisations keep the record. Ending access that has already ended changes nothing.

get.description: Lists every division and department of the organization with its parent, Site Limit, site counts and member count, and whether you can manage each one. The count for a department includes the departments inside it.

post.description: Adds a division or department, optionally inside another. Only an organization owner or admin can add one. Departments go four levels deep at most, and a division cannot sit inside a department.

put.description: Renames a department or moves it inside another. A department admin can rename their own department. Moving one in the tree is for organization owners and admins.

delete.description: Deletes a department and its member roles. It is refused while the department still holds sites or other departments. Only an organization owner or admin can delete one.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Lists the people with a role in the department and the role each one holds.

post.description: Gives a member of the organization a role in the department. The role covers the departments inside it too. You can give only a role that carries nothing you do not hold yourself.

delete.description: Takes a person out of the department. They stay in the organization. You cannot remove a role that carries something you do not hold yourself.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

put.description: Changes the role a person holds in the department. You can change a role only when both the current and the new role carry nothing you do not hold yourself.

Sets how many sites a department can hold, counting the departments inside it, or removes the limit with null. Only an organization owner or admin can set it. A limit below the current count stops new sites and removes none.

post.summary: Create a site in a department
post.description: Starts a site create and places the new site in the department in the path. The Site Limit of the department and of each department above it counts every site below it, and a create over the limit is refused. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.description: Lists the organization sites with the department each one sits in, or none for a site at the organization level.

Reads what the organisation in the path may do on its current plan. A null limit is unknown or negotiated and counts as no allowance. Only an activated subscription changes the plan; every other account reads as the free plan. billingAccount is true when the organisation has a Stripe customer, so the billing portal can open for it. credits holds the units bought in one-time packs per meter, with zeros left out.

post.summary: Import a site from a server
post.description: Starts the import of the server checked by the survey operation in the body into a new managed site and returns its operation. The engine copies the database over one read-only connection, converts it, creates the site on a Drupflare address, loads the copy, checks that the site answers, then deletes the key and the copies. The server is never changed. A database above the restore limit, or a survey that found a blocker, is refused with a plain reason before anything is created. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. It needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up.

post.summary: Make a key for an import
post.description: Makes a one-time key for the server in the body and returns the public line to add to its authorized keys. The key lasts 24 hours and is deleted when the import ends. The private half is stored sealed and is never returned. It needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up.

post.summary: Read or confirm the host key of a server
post.description: Connects to the server of the key in the body, reads the host key it presents and stops before any login, so no command runs. Without confirm it returns the key type and fingerprint to show the owner. With confirm.fingerprint it reads the key again and stores it only when it matches, then every later connection must present that key. It needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up.

post.summary: Check a server before an import
post.description: Starts a read-only check of the Drupal site at the path on the server of the key in the body and returns its operation. The host key must be confirmed first. Nothing on the server is changed. When the operation succeeds, its cursor is a JSON record whose dossier field holds the verdict, the refusals, the size estimate and the findings. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. It needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up.

get.description: Lists the invitations that are waiting to be accepted. The invitation link is never shown again after the email is sent.

post.description: Emails an invitation to join the organization with a role. The link works once and expires after seven days. Owners cannot be invited, and only an owner can invite an admin.
Sends the invitation again with a new link and a new seven day expiry. The link from the earlier email stops working.
Stops an invitation from being accepted. The link in the email no longer works.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Lists the members of the organization in the path with their role and the day they joined. Pass the last id from a page as cursor to read the next one.

delete.description: Removes a member from the organization. You cannot remove someone whose role is above yours, and the last owner cannot be removed. Removing yourself leaves the organization.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.description: Removes one person everywhere in the organization in one step: their membership and department roles, their site access, the agency access and invitations they created, their keys and their service accounts. With dryRun it lists what would happen and changes nothing. Running it for real needs a fresh sign-in. The last owner cannot be offboarded.

put.description: Sets the role of a member. You can give only roles you hold yourself, and only an owner can give the admin role. The last owner cannot be demoted.

get.description: Lists the paired nodes of the organisation in the path in id order, with their host facts and when each last reported.
Reads one paired node of the organisation in the path.

post.description: Cuts the link to a node. The server refuses everything the node sends and sends it nothing. The box keeps running on its own, and it can be paired again with a new pairing. Revoking a node that is already revoked changes nothing.

post.summary: Create a site on a node
post.description: Asks a paired, connected node to add a Drupal site on a host name it will serve, and returns the operation. The box holds the request for its operator to approve, so the operation can wait. The site is listed once the box has added it. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.
Creates a pairing that lasts 15 minutes and returns its claim token once. Run bastion pair with the address on the box. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Returns one operation of the organisation in the path, with its steps in the order the steps run.

post.description: Starts the same work again as a new operation that carries the failed one in retryOf, and returns it. The request has no body. Only an operation that failed can be retried, and only for site creates, site updates, backups, restores and cleanups; any other type answers 422 with a plain reason. A failed create cleans up its earlier attempt first and then creates the site again under the same name. The caller needs the permission the operation was first started with. A retry that is already running or has succeeded is returned instead of starting another. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: List the pilots of an organisation
get.description: Lists the pilots of the organisation, oldest first, with their assigned sites.

post.description: Starts a pilot with its baseline. The success criteria are the words the owner writes; nothing is filled in for them.

get.description: Shows one pilot with its baseline, success criteria, sites and decision.

put.description: Changes the fields sent. A field left out keeps its stored value. A decided pilot keeps its start date.

put.summary: Record the decision on a pilot
put.description: Records whether the organisation continues, extends or stops, and what it would pay to continue. A stop is recorded the same way as a continue.

get.summary: Download the pilot observations as CSV
get.description: Streams every observation of the pilot as CSV, in the order recorded. Text cells that start with a formula character are prefixed with an apostrophe.

post.description: Adds an exception, failure, unsupported item, manual task or note to the pilot. Failures and unsupported items stay in the report.

get.description: Assembles the report: what the old hosting cost, what Drupflare cost where a figure exists, the manual work and its minutes, failures, unsupported items and exceptions. Negative results are included.

put.summary: Set the sites of a pilot
put.description: Replaces the list of sites in the pilot. Each site must belong to the organisation.

get.description: Lists the Cloudflare accounts the organisation connected, oldest first, with each connection state, what its token can do and when it was last checked. A connection never shows its stored token.

post.description: Checks the token, and stores one only if it can edit Workers scripts. When the token can make other tokens, Drupflare makes a narrower one for this account, keeps only that, and does not keep the one you gave. Otherwise it keeps the token you gave. The stored token is sealed and never returned. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused.

delete.description: Wipes the stored token. When Drupflare made the token, it also asks Cloudflare to delete it; the narrower token has no permission to manage tokens, so Cloudflare may refuse, and the answer says whether you must delete it yourself. Sites that run on the account refuse the revoke unless force lists each site ID. A second revoke changes nothing. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

post.description: Checks the stored token against Cloudflare and records what it can do now. A token that expired or lost the permission to edit Workers scripts marks the connection invalid. A check that gets no answer from Cloudflare changes nothing. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused.

post.summary: Check what a Cloudflare token can do
post.description: Reads what the token can see and do on the account it names. Nothing is stored and the token is not returned. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Lists the policy groups of the organization with their rules and what each one is assigned to, and the default group picked for each data classification label.

post.description: Adds a policy group with its rules. A group does nothing until it is assigned to the organization, a department, a site or a data classification.

put.description: Replaces the name and rules of a policy group. The change applies to everything the group is assigned to from the next request.

delete.description: Deletes a policy group. It is refused while the group is still assigned to the organization, a department, a site or a classification label.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

post.description: Applies a policy group to the organization, a department, a site or a data classification label. Everything below a department inherits it. A label has one default group, so picking a new one replaces the old one.

delete.description: Takes a policy group off the organization, a department, a site or a classification label. For the organization, the target is the organization id.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

put.description: Sets what the organization calls one of the four data classification labels, such as its own level names, or clears the name with null.

get.summary: List the procurement records of an organisation
get.description: Lists quotes, purchase orders, invoices and contracts, oldest first. Amounts are the text the buyer entered.

post.description: Adds a quote, purchase order, invoice or contract. Nothing here computes a total or a tax.

put.description: Replaces the fields of one procurement record in the organisation.

get.summary: Download the procurement records as CSV
get.description: Streams every procurement record of the organisation as CSV. Text cells that start with a formula character are prefixed with an apostrophe.
Lists the provider connections of the organisation in the path, active and revoked, oldest first. A connection never shows its stored credential.

post.description: GitHub and GitLab answer with a redirect address on the provider, where the person picks what to share; finish with the complete route when the provider returns. Bitbucket, Gitea and Forgejo take a read-only token and answer with the stored connection. The token is sealed and never shown again. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

get.summary: List the repositories of a connection
get.description: Asks the provider which repositories the connection can read, up to 100. A GitHub installation lists only the repositories it was installed on. A revoked connection is refused.

post.description: Revokes the connection in the path and clears its stored credential in the same write. A second revoke answers the same view. Remotes that use it stop pulling. A GitHub installation is removed from the GitHub side in GitHub settings. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

Finishes a GitHub or GitLab connection with what the provider sent back. The state must be the one this organisation started, and it works once. For GitHub the installation must be one the signed-in person can reach on GitHub. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Lists the access reviews of the organization, newest first, with how many items each has and how many are still waiting. Owners and admins see every item. A department admin sees only the reviews with items in their own departments, and the counts cover only those items. Anyone else is refused.

post.description: Opens a review of the whole organization or of one department and its sub-departments. It takes a copy of the people, grants, agency access, keys and service accounts in scope as they are now. Changes made later do not alter the copy.

get.description: Returns one review with the items, the decision on each and whether it is about you. Owners and admins see every item. A department admin sees only the items they can decide in their own departments, and the review is limited to those. Nobody can decide an item about themselves.

post.description: Carries out every removal still waiting and closes the review. Every item needs a decision first. A removal that fails is recorded on its item and the review still closes.

post.summary: Decide one item in a review
post.description: Keeps or removes one item. Owners and admins decide any item. A department admin decides only items inside their own departments, and only while the organization setting allows it. A removal is carried out when the review closes, or right away when applyNow is true, which only an owner or admin can ask for. You cannot decide an item about yourself.

get.summary: Export the evidence of a closed review
get.description: Returns a closed review as JSON, or as CSV with format=csv. Both carry the SHA-256 of the CSV, so a copy can be checked later. Text cells that start with a formula character are prefixed with an apostrophe.
Shows how often a review opens by itself: every quarter, every year or never, and when the last one opened.

put.description: Sets how often a review of the whole organization opens by itself. The first one opens after a full interval has passed.

get.description: Lists the keys, service accounts and site grants that have not been used for 90 days. A key or account that was never used counts from the day it was made. A grant keeps no use record, so it is listed by age alone.
Lists the service accounts you can manage in the organization, with the owner, the expiry and when any key last worked. A department admin sees only the accounts in their own department.

post.description: Creates a service account that has no sign-in and holds only keys. It needs a named owner who belongs to the organization and an expiry of at most one year. Its keys never carry more than the owner holds.
Revokes every key of the service account and turns the account off. Disabling an account that is already off changes nothing.

get.summary: List the keys of a service account
get.description: Lists every key issued to the service account, newest first, with the permissions it carries and when it last worked.

post.summary: Create a key for a service account
post.description: Creates a key for the service account and returns its token once. The key can hold only permissions that the account owner holds, it loses any permission the owner loses, and it never outlives the account. It needs a signed-in session with a fresh sign-in, so an API key is refused.

get.description: Returns the organization settings. Today that is whether department admins can decide access review items.

put.description: Sets whether department admins can decide access review items. Owners and admins change it. Turning it off keeps every decision already made and stops department admins from making new ones. The change is audited with the old and new value.

get.description: Lists the sites of the organisation in the path in id order. Sites still being created are left out; read their operation instead.

post.description: Starts a site create in the organisation in the path and returns its operation. The site ID is the operation target. The site is listed once its create finishes. A custom site takes the bundleId of a bundle the organisation uploaded and no other kind takes one. A self-managed site names a Cloudflare connection of the organisation with connectionId and runs at the account workers.dev address, or at customHost, a hostname on a zone the connection can route with that zone ID. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: Read who can open a site
get.description: Lists the active access rules of the site in the path, which access types the plan includes, and the invited address limit. Passwords and link tokens are never returned.

post.summary: Add an access rule to a site
post.description: Adds one rule to the production site or one of its environments. Rules combine, so a visitor who matches any of them gets in. A password or review link is stored as a hash; a review link token is returned once, in this response.

delete.summary: Remove an access rule from a site
delete.description: Removes one rule and starts the change that applies it to the site. Visitors who got in through it lose access when the site next renews its lease. The response names the operation to follow.

post.summary: Apply the saved access rules to a site again
post.description: Starts the change that writes the saved access rules to the site. Use it when a rule is saved but the site has not picked it up. The response names the operation to follow.

Starts the move of the self-managed site in the path to a new managed site and returns its operation. The engine copies the site's database, creates the managed site on a Drupflare address, restores the copy into it and checks that it answers. The source site is never changed or deleted, and the managed copy is one-way. A database above the restore limit stops the operation with a plain reason before anything is created. The request has no body and needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site was already adopted or another change to it is running, 422 when the site is not self-managed or not live, and 403 when the plan has no room for another site.

get.summary: List the backups of a site
get.description: Lists the backups of the site in the path, newest first. A backup too large for a restore says why and can still be exported.

post.description: Starts a backup of the site in the path and returns its operation. The dump is stored without secrets. A backup reads verified false until a scratch restore has proved it. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.description: Streams the backup as one SQL file. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused. The dump carries no secrets. A backup of another organisation is not found. An audit row is written before the download starts.

post.summary: Restore a backup into a site
post.description: Starts a restore of the backup in the path into another site of the same organisation, or the same site, and returns its operation. The restore replaces the target database. A backup that is too large for a restore is refused. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

Restores the backup in the path into a scratch copy, checks that the copy answers, removes the copy and marks the backup verified. The live site is not touched. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: Read the spend budget of a site
get.description: Reads the budget that applies to one site. Under a pooled allowance a site has a default share until the owner sets one, and ownerSet says which it is. A site without a budget of its own is governed by the organisation budget and reads null percent. A free organisation answers not_applicable.

put.summary: Set the spend budget of a site
put.description: Sets the budget of one site as a percent of its monthly allowance. It cannot be higher than the organisation budget. Lowering it, or switching from alert to block, needs the billing permission. Raising it, or switching from block to alert, also needs a fresh sign-in. Every change is audited with the old and new values.

post.summary: Update a custom site to an uploaded bundle
post.description: Starts an update of the custom site in the path to a bundle the organisation uploaded and returns its operation. The new bundle keeps the stores the site already uses and only adds migration steps; a bundle that removes or renames a class the site stores data in is refused with 422 and the reason. The site keeps serving while the engine uploads the bundle, checks the site, and puts the earlier bundle back if the check fails. An earlier bundle can be put back later with the rollback route. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site already runs that bundle or another change to it is running, 422 when the site is not live or the bundle is not one of the organisation's uploads, and 403 when the plan does not include custom code.

get.summary: Read the data classification of a site
get.description: Returns the label of the site, or null when it has none.

put.summary: Set the data classification of a site
put.description: Labels the site public, internal, restricted or regulated, or clears the label with null. The label picks the default policy group of the site.

post.summary: Clean up a site that failed to create
post.description: Removes what a failed create left behind for the site in the path and returns the cleanup operation, whose type is repair.run. The site must never have become active; a live site answers 409. It also answers 409 while another change to the site is running. The operation stops the site serving, deletes its script, routes and resources, frees its name and marks the site deleted. A repeat on a site that is already clean returns the operation that cleaned it. The request has no body. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

put.summary: Add a site to a client
put.description: Groups a site of this organisation under a client. A site sits under one client at a time.

delete.summary: Remove a site from a client
delete.description: Takes a site out of a client grouping. The site stays in the organisation.

get.summary: Read the plan and state of a site move
get.description: Returns whether the site can take a move, the expected write window of each write policy, the four points at which the new site is checked, and the latest move on the site with its steps, its write count and whether going back is still a DNS reversal. A site that has had no move has no latest move.

post.summary: Start moving a site by cutover
post.description: Starts the move of the address in the body from the source server to the managed site in the path, and returns its operation. The body names the source, the address that moves and how the source treats writes while the move runs: freeze (maintenance page), read-only (the site serves and refuses writes) or delta (a short freeze for the last copy). The move waits for the owner's approval before it touches the source's writes, and it never deletes the source. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Answers 409 when another change to the site is running, 422 when the site is not a live managed site, and 501 until moves are available.

Approves the move that is waiting for the owner. Approval lets the move apply the write policy to the source, copy the last changes, promote the new site and point the address at it. The request has no body and needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Answers 409 when the move is not waiting for approval or is no longer running.

get.summary: Download the changes the new site took
get.description: Streams the changes the new site accepted since the move as one SQL file, written for a MySQL or MariaDB database. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused. Answers 404 until a move has saved its changes. An audit row is written before the download starts.

post.summary: Choose how a site move ends
post.description: Sends a decision to the move that is observing the new site. rollback asks for a DNS reversal, which the move allows only while the new site has accepted no writes. keep-new, abandon-new-data and export-changes are the three choices once it has. The move reads the write count itself and records a refusal that the next read of the move shows. The body names one value; the request needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Answers 409 when the move is not observing the new site.

Starts the delete of the site in the path and returns its operation. The body names the site: confirm must equal the site's name. The site stops serving once the operation tombstones it, and its address is held for 90 days. Backups are kept. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 while another change to the site is running.

put.summary: Move a site to a department
put.description: Places the site in a department, or back at the organization level with null. You need to be able to add sites to the department you move it into, and the Site Limits on the way up still apply. Only an organization owner or admin can take a site out of every department.

get.summary: Read the custom domains of a site
get.description: Returns whether the site can take a custom domain, the domains that serve it now, and the latest attach with its four stages (ownership, certificate, routing, final check), the DNS records the owner must add and the plain reason it stopped. A site that has had no attach has no latest attach.

post.summary: Attach a custom domain to a site
post.description: Starts attaching the domain in the body to the managed site in the path, and returns its operation. The attach moves through four stages in order: ownership of the domain, the certificate, routing, and a final check that the site answers on the domain. It waits on the DNS records the owner adds, which the read route lists. A domain under drupflare.app or drupflare.com is refused, and so is a domain another site holds. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up. Answers 409 when another change to the site is running and 422 when the site is not a live managed site or the domain is not valid.

post.summary: Check the DNS records for a custom domain
post.description: Lists the DNS records the owner adds for the domain in the body and reads each one live, without starting an attach. Each record is found, not found yet, found with a different value, or could not be checked right now; a DNS lookup that fails is never reported as a missing record. The answer also lists hazards: an alias record on a bare domain, other records that point the name elsewhere, CAA records that block the certificate, and a second ownership value. A domain under drupflare.app or drupflare.com is refused, and so is a wildcard. A domain another site holds comes back with held set and no records. Needs a signed-in session. Answers 422 when the site is not a live managed site or the domain is not valid.

post.summary: Cancel a custom domain that is still waiting
post.description: Gives up the domain in the body for the managed site in the path while it waits for the owner or is parked. A running attach stops at its next look and reads as cancelled. The name is free for any site to claim afterwards. A domain that is already set up cannot be cancelled here and answers 409. A repeat, or a domain this site does not hold, answers 200 with released false. Needs a signed-in session with a recent step-up.

get.summary: List the environments of a site
get.description: Lists the staging, dev and preview environments of the site, newest first. A preview carries the time it is deleted at; a staging or dev copy carries none.

post.description: Creates a staging or dev copy of the site from its newest restorable backup, or from the backup named in the body. The copy gets its own database and files and its own owner token; the original is not changed. Settings and secrets stay behind and must be set again on the copy. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

delete.description: Removes the environment copy and everything the platform made for it. The original site is not touched. An environment that is still being created or deleted is refused. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: Read the state of the first admin password
get.description: Says whether the first admin password can still be revealed, without revealing it. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused, and the answer is never cached. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.description: Returns the admin password the new site generated, once. It needs a signed-in session, so an API key is refused. A second call, an expired password and a site of another organisation are all not found. Do not send an Idempotency-Key header: a replayed answer would store the password.

get.description: Lists the people who have a role on this site, with the role and any expiry. A grant that was revoked does not appear.

post.summary: Give a person a site role
post.description: Gives an existing account a role on this site: site admin, maintainer or viewer, with an optional expiry. The person must already have an account. Someone who already has a role on the site is changed instead.

put.description: Changes the role or the expiry of one collaborator on this site. The change applies from the next request the person makes.

delete.description: Ends one person's role on this site. Revoking a role that already ended changes nothing.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.summary: Read the health of a site
get.description: Reads the site live through its own hostname and returns its health tree, whether it answers, and the readiness checks. The answer is kept for 15 seconds per site. A site that does not answer is reported as not responding, not as an error. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Deliver an edit to a Drupal site
post.description: Sends the files of one custom module, theme or profile to the site and returns the operation. The files are the whole set: any file of that module the request leaves out is removed from the site. Paths must sit in modules/custom/<name>/, themes/custom/<name>/ or profiles/custom/<name>/, and each file is text, given as plain text or base64. A restore point is taken first, the site boots the new files and puts the old ones back if they fail, and a passing edit is added to the code history with its files so it can be rolled back to. Refused with 422 when the site is not an active Drupal site, when Drupflare holds no access to it, when the plan does not include custom code, or when a path or file is not allowed. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Roll a site back to an earlier edit
post.description: Sends the stored files of an earlier edit to the site again and returns the operation. Only the module, theme or profile that edit delivered goes back; the data and the other code stay as they are. The entry is named by its id from the code history, and it must be an edit that kept its files. The data version guard that applies to a release rollback applies here too. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: Search the modules for a site
get.description: Searches the module list by machine name and label, filtered by state and kind. Each row carries its state and reason. installed is null when the site cannot say whether a module is installed. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Check whether a module can be installed on a site
post.description: Asks the site whether it can take a module from the list. Names any conflict with the code the site already has. Nothing is installed and nothing on the site changes. A site that cannot be asked gets a plain refusal, not an error. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Enable an installed module or theme
post.description: Starts turning on a module or theme that is already on the site and returns its operation. A restore point is taken before anything changes, and the site is checked afterward. A theme is enabled the same way. A module that cannot run here and one on no list are refused. Strata on the free plan is refused until the request carries confirm: true, once per site. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Install a module or theme on a site
post.description: Starts an install of a module or theme from the list and returns its operation. The site is checked again first, and a restore point is taken before anything changes. A module that has never run on a site needs confirm set to true. A module that ships with every site, one that cannot run here, and one on no list are refused. Installing does not enable. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Remove a module from a site
post.description: Starts removing a module and returns its operation. The site names the modules that need it first, and the removal is refused while any of them is enabled. A restore point is taken before anything changes. The site uninstalls the module first, and its files go only after that works. A module that ships with every site cannot be removed. Answers 422 with the reason while the site cannot remove modules yet. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Make a theme the default or admin theme
post.description: Starts a change of the default or the admin theme of the site and returns its operation. The theme has to be enabled first. A restore point is taken before anything changes, and the site is asked afterward which theme it uses. Answers 422 with the reason while the site cannot change themes yet. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

Creates a temporary copy of the site from its newest restorable backup, or from the backup named in the body. The copy is deleted when its time runs out, three days after it is made unless the body names another number of hours (at most 336). A site holds a limited number of previews at once. The copy gets its own database, files and owner token; the original is not changed. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: List the repositories attached to a site
get.description: Lists the remotes of the site in the path with the result of the last pull on each. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Attach a repository to a site
post.description: Attaches one branch of a repository, through an active connection of the organisation, to the site in the path. The mount path must sit inside modules, themes or profiles. The interval is in minutes, from 5, and defaults to 60.

post.summary: Pull a repository onto a site
post.description: Starts a pull of the attached repository onto the site in the path and returns its operation. The result is written on the remote as its last pull. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

post.summary: Rename a site found on a box
post.description: Changes the name of a site a box reported and the dashboard listed. It is the only kind of site that can be renamed, since the name of any other site is part of its address. The name is 1 to 100 characters and no other live site of the organisation holds it.

get.summary: List the automatic repairs of a site
get.description: Lists the automatic repairs made on the site in the path, newest first, with what was seen before and after each one and whether Undo is offered.

post.description: Starts the undo of the repair in the path and returns its operation. The undo is itself listed in the site repairs. A repair that cannot be undone is refused with the reason. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: List the restore points of a site
get.description: Lists the saved copies of the site, newest first, each with what it restores and what it does not. Point-in-time recovery is listed once as a layer with its window, not as one row per moment. A copy counts as verified only after a test restore passes.

post.summary: Restore a site to an earlier moment
post.description: Schedules a point-in-time restore of everything the site stores. The site applies it the next time it starts. The moment must be in the past and inside the recovery window. The operation keeps an undo bookmark that returns the site to where it was. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: List the code history of a site
get.description: Lists the releases the site has run, newest first, up to 50. Each row carries the release id and version, a note when the revision is an edit, and whether it is the code the site runs now. A site of another organisation is not found.

post.summary: Roll a site back to an earlier release
post.description: Puts the code of an earlier registered release back on the site and returns the operation. The data is not rolled back, so the request is refused with 422 and the offers "restore-data-with-code" and "fix-forward" when the current release changed how the site stores its data, or when the data version is unknown. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site already runs that release or another change to it is running.

get.summary: Check whether a site can roll back its code
get.description: Compares the data version of the site in the path with the release named in the release query parameter. Answers whether the code alone can go back to that release. When it cannot, the answer says why and offers restoring the data together with the code, or fixing the problem in a new release. Answers 404 when the release is not registered and 422 when it is a different kind of release than the site runs.

get.summary: Read the settings of a site
get.description: Reads the effective settings of the site in the path with where each value comes from. Only the groups the caller may read are returned. Send fresh=1 to skip the stored copy. A site that does not answer returns the last settings it reported, marked stale, or an empty state. A site of another organisation is not found.

put.summary: Change the settings of a site
put.description: Starts a change of one or more settings of the site in the path and returns its operation. The caller needs the write permission of every group a setting belongs to. Each value is checked against what the site accepts, and the operation writes it, reads it back and records the change in the settings history. Send the etag from the settings read; a site that changed since answers 409 with the current values. A setting the platform sets, one set at deploy time, or one only an owner may change is refused with 422. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: List the settings changes of a site
get.description: Lists the settings changes made through the platform for the site in the path, newest first. Only changes to settings of a group the caller may read are listed, and a secret shows only whether it was set. A change says whether the site reported the new value back and whether it can be reverted.

post.description: Starts a change that puts every setting of the named change back to what it held before, and returns its operation. The caller needs the write permission of every group the settings belong to, and the same checks as a new change apply. A change that was already reverted answers 409. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation.

get.summary: Read the Strata allocation for a site
get.description: Returns how much of the site allowance Strata may use: the setting, whether it records statements, how often history is saved in seconds, whether the site has accepted it, and when the free plan warning was confirmed. A site that never chose gets light.

put.summary: Set the Strata allocation for a site
put.description: Sets how much of the site allowance Strata may use: light records changes made through the site, and detailed also records every database statement and uses about twice as much. History is saved every 15 minutes either way. The free plan allows light only. The change is recorded and audited, and the status shows whether the site has accepted it.

post.description: Proposes that the site moves to another organisation. The receiving organisation answers within 14 days, and the site stays here until it accepts. Ownership, billing and any agency access move as separate steps. Keeping an agency maintainer access needs that access to be active for this site.
Withdraws a proposed transfer while the receiving organisation has not answered. Once it has answered, the transfer cannot be cancelled.

post.summary: Update a site to the current release
post.description: Starts an update of the site in the path to the platform's current release and returns its operation. The platform picks the target; the request has no body. The site keeps serving while the engine uploads the new release, checks the site, and puts the old release back if the check fails. Send an Idempotency-Key header; a repeat returns the same operation. Answers 409 when the site already runs the current release or another change to it is running, and 422 when the site is not live.

get.summary: Read the views of a site for one month
get.description: Shows the views of one site for one UTC month, per day, with the accounting state of each day. A site of another organisation is not found.

Shows how people at the organisation sign in through its own identity provider: the provider address, the client id, the allowed email domains, the role mapping and whether it is on. The client secret never comes back; the answer only says whether one is stored.

put.description: Saves the identity provider settings for the organisation. Leave the client secret out to keep the stored one. Turning sign-in on needs a passing test of the saved settings, and mails the organisation owners. A sign-in claim can map to viewer, developer, billing or admin and never to owner.

post.description: Reads the identity provider discovery document and one key set with the saved settings. Nobody signs in. A pass is recorded and allows turning sign-in on.

get.description: Lists the times you let Drupflare support into this organization, newest first, with whether each one is still live.

post.description: Gives Drupflare support time-boxed access to this organization, for 1 hour up to 7 days. Needs step-up. Support never reads site content. Every use shows in your audit log, and you can revoke the grant at any time.

delete.description: Ends a support access grant now. Support loses access on the next request. Revoking a grant that already ended does nothing.

204.description: Done. The response has no body.

get.description: Lists the transfers this organisation proposed and the transfers waiting for its answer. A proposal that passed its window shows as expired.

post.description: Accepts a site proposed to this organisation. The receiving organisation must have room for another site on its plan, and the answer names the limit when it has none.

Starts the handover of an accepted site to this organisation: its records are copied, ownership, billing and designated access change, and the routing epoch rises so an old lease cannot serve. The answer carries the operation; the transfer reads completing, then completed or failed. After a failed run, call again to start the next attempt.
Declines a site proposed to this organisation. The site stays with the proposing organisation, and a declined transfer cannot be accepted later.

get.summary: Read the views of an organisation for one month
get.description: Shows the views of each site and of the whole organisation for one UTC month, per day, with the accounting state of each day. A started hour with no stored row is unaccounted, never zero.

post.summary: Read what a site shows from outside
post.description: Reads the home page of a public site and up to three small files on the same host, then reports the system and version the site discloses, where it appears to be hosted and what it could not tell. It never says a site is compatible. A refusal names the reason in details.reason.

get.description: Returns one site of your organisation. A site still being created is not found.

get.summary: List the operations of a site
get.description: Lists the operations of one site, newest first, in pages of up to 100.

Lists the site templates with their category, whether they are free and whether they can be used now. Disabled templates carry a Coming Soon label. The Drupal templates built from the corpus are listed apart, each with its build state, any security advisories its Drupal core carries, any patch that did not apply, and whether it fits the Free plan.
Lists the documents on the trust center that are published and not retired. Drafts and retired documents never appear here.
Streams one published trust document as an attachment. The stored file is looked up by the document id, never by a path from the request.
Redirects to the page that asks you to confirm. Reading the link changes nothing, so a mail scanner that opens it does not unsubscribe anyone.

post.summary: Stop one kind of optional mail
post.description: Switches off the one category named in the signed link from an email. The link carries the token in its query; a mail client posts the one-click form to it and the body is ignored. Essential mail has no link. Using a link again changes nothing.

session.name: __Host-drupflare_session
session.description: The session cookie set at sign-in.

apiKey.description: An API key that starts with dfk_. An action that needs a signed-in session or a fresh sign-in refuses keys.

ContractHeader.name: Drupflare-Contract
ContractHeader.description: The contract versions the client understands, as common=<min>-<max>. A server that cannot serve the range answers 426.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Repeat a write safely. The same key with the same request returns the first result.

RequestId.description: The id of this request. Quote it when you contact support.

Contract.description: The contract versions this server supports, as common=<min>-<max>.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the window frees a slot.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before the next request.

BadRequest.description: The request is invalid. details.issues lists each field path.

Unauthenticated.description: The request has no valid session or API key.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not do this.

Unprocessable.description: The Idempotency-Key was used for a different request.

ContractUnsupported.description: The server does not support the requested contract range. details.supported names the range it does.

InternalError.description: The server failed. Quote the requestId when you report it.
